findings.claim: Who reviews the one change R-10 creates? One maintainer, in one sitting. The change now carries the move, 12 round-1 wording fixes, the R-12 schema and renderer field, the R-13 rename and check, the R-11 oracle slot, and this round's findings. A human verdict gets worse as the batch grows, and that is the one case where batch size still matters when generation is cheap. Splitting is ruled out (R-10), so shrink the batch by deleting text. Seven of the nine derivatives rows (Agile rituals, story points, sprint cadence, pair programming, ITIL bureaucracy, process maturity, and the Amara and Braudel frame at :14-18) have no reader: no persona or skill file mentions story points, pair programming, ITIL, Amara or Braudel. Only the pyramid row (test-strategy-advisor), line-by-line review (chorus-review SKILL.md) and root cause (BINDINGS.md) land on a lens. Deleting the rest also makes F20 (the DORA wording at :85) moot, along with part of F8, so those fixes never have to be written or reviewed. Keep three derivatives rows, move the frame to the 10x test alone, and leave the history in docs/ for the maintainer if wanted.

findings.claim: Where does the note put the bottleneck? It names two places. :31 says it 'becomes what to read' (C1), and :41-42 says the share spent on validation 'keeps rising' (C8). Both are trends, not a location. A lens that acts on a trend invests in validation everywhere. A lens that acts on a location asks where the slowest trustworthy verdict sits today, here, and only then prices work. In this project the evidence puts it at the one maintainer's attention, not at missing oracles. Fix: keep the asymmetry as a hypothesis and add one sentence. 'This says where to look first, not where the constraint is. Find it in the project's evidence before a finding leans on it.' Without that sentence, C8 becomes a licence to gold-plate verification.

findings.claim: Half right. Proportions tuned to authoring cost are a derivative. But the pyramid also rests on time-to-red (C7: milliseconds, inside the loop) and on what a red names (C2: one function fits a slot, an end-to-end chain does not); 10x cheaper code changes neither. It also stops short of F15: tests are the callable oracle for verification (C8) and never close validation, and no row says so, so the 10x test can file the whole portfolio as derivative. Fix: tuned to 'authoring cost (falling) plus run time and diagnosis (not falling)'; survives as 'which risk does this catch that nothing cheaper would, and what does its red name?'; add a practice row, automated checks as the verification oracle (C7, C8).

derived.claim: F1(b) and F12 put PC ids into evidence refs. vocab.schema.json declares itself the single home of every closed vocabulary, so the reflex will be a PC enum there to validate refs. That is a duplicate authority: the id set would then be authored in the PROCESS-CONSTANTS.md table and in vocab, and validate.mjs would reject records over an advisory text (R-2), turning advice into a record contract. Ruling: no enum. The note's table is the sole author of the id set, refs stay free strings, and resolution is checked in canon by the FC1 extension. A record id that dangles is a NEED_INFO for the lens, not a schema error.
